channel.description: Recent content in Postcps on Of All The Blogs

item.title: The Truth
item.description: Friends, I have something to tell you. All of you. I take no pleasure in revealing it, but there are some things which can’t be kept hidden. I’ve kept this from you all. But I am not here to make excuses, or to even explain myself. I just want to tell the truth. And there’s a lot to tell, too much for this website’s normal post format to take. I’m serious, when I finally compiled it all into something I was happy with (well, not happy per se, but… you know what I mean), the budget server I and Adrianne share didn’t have enough space on its drive.

item.title: Assignment season strikes again
item.description: Just when the seasonal depression lifts, assignment season swoops in to replace it. When will it end? In reality, it ends in about 10 days for me. But for now, I’d like to be dramatic about it. And why is it too that the weather is absolutely amazing when you’re studying but it rains as soon as you finish your last exam? These are the questions that need to be asked.

item.title: bad weather for ducks
item.description: What a suddenly beautiful day today is! I sat out for a good two hours this afternoon, photosynthesizing to my hearts content. Does you wonders, sunlight. Helps you forget your woes, like the vicious rotting-egg-stink that will not lift from your house’s kitchen. The less said of it the better. I made my triumphant return to the gym today. And by triumphant, I mean that I really didn’t want to, and I’d slept in so I felt groggy, and since it’s been a month since I last went I had to drop my weights on several exercises and felt embarrassed despite the fact that no one around me knew what weight I’d been doing before anyway…

item.title: Some Good News (not from me)
item.description: The news is never really very happy, is it? As in THE news, not just news. Most of the time, news is in the news because it’s bad news. This fact is quite depressing. So today I’d like to just share some good news. Like your daily news update, but only good stuff. For a start, the world record for the longest plank has been beaten by a 58-year-old grandmother of 12.

item.title: Hehehe
item.description: I have naught to say this week, but a promise is a promise, so I post nonetheless. In any case, here’s a funny stand-up show I saw, with an important message for us all:

item.title: Blog, blog, the rattlin’ blog
item.description: Missed me? No that’s alright you don’t have to answer that. Been a little while, hasn’t it? I can only apologize. And provide Adrianne with, what at the point must surely be, a lifetime supply of drinks. I won’t go into why this little absence started initially, other than to say that group projects suck. I’m actually in the Netherlands as I write this, in Rotterdam. It’s been a weird family holiday, not just because it’s been a minute since we did this, all five of us.

item.title: Cindy
item.description: Well it’s been a while. Nice to meet again. It’s been a weird few weeks. As a first post back, I just want to dedicate it to my little westie Cindy who passed away last week. She was truly the best dog ever. She had a long and full life at 15 years old so I’m just very thankful for how long we had with her. Cindy had a pretty wild last day.

item.title: The Water We Swim In
item.description: I have been busy this week. What a stock phrase that is, and for most of you not at all unusual, but it is for me. I am not used to being busy. I am not used to doing a great many things at any time. I also have a terrible habit of praying for specific things and forgetting that I did, and I have a sinking feeling that a month or two ago I asked God that I might be stretched more than I have been recently.

item.title: Wisdom
item.description: I’ve never seen a purple cow I never wish to see one But I can tell you anyhow I’d rather see than be one

item.title: Lent
item.description: Lent this year has come up really suddenly. It’s like one minute I was talking about all the things I wanted to do with Lent and the next I’m actually having to do them. Imagine that. Honestly, I feel a lot less willing to do anything for Lent this year. Last year was the first time I’d actually done something for it and I really appreciated it. This year, I just don’t really want to give anything up.

item.title: How does God speak to us?
item.description: I’ve kinda struggled with this recently. I grew up in a pretty traditional Christian home so I really hadn’t thought about it much. I thought that God only spoke through the words written in His word, the Bible. But recently I’ve just come to the sorta realisation that God communicates with us in loads of ways. When i say realisation, i mean that God keeps speaking to me and i keep ignoring it.

item.title: The Good Week
item.description: I’ve written on driving several times before now, and my valiant efforts to learn in the face of fear. Well this Tuesday was my test. A test a long time in the making – I passed my theory over a year and a half ago – and needless to say I was quite on the edge for the whole day leading up to it. Mine was to take place at ten to three, a fairly busy time of day.

item.title: ”Add title”
item.description: My mind is having many thoughts. Not many useful ones as I try to come up with a topic to write about this week. But many thoughts are occurring. I guess the main thought that I’m having is that I have no thoughts. But then again, that is a thought. Therefore, I do have thoughts, just not ones that I want to have. As Descartes once described it “I think therefore I am”.

item.title: Sneak preview
item.description: The following is a short, teasing excerpt from my first successfully completed fictional work. It’s a period piece, a novella set in 1920’s London that follows a family among the upper echelons of society as they slowly come to terms with a rapidly changing society. Please enjoy. “Balderdash, Marjory, you can’t have foei-gras without a jus!” I hope you’ve had your literary sensibilities tantalized by this (admittedly, perhaps, rather over-large) extract from my upcoming magnum-opus.

item.title: thinkful thoughts
item.description: i have many thoughts today. i think, in fact, that the thoughts might have thoughts themselves. here, have three of them: it’s so easy to believe that focus will come to us (or become us) when we need it, as we sit down at out desk/steering wheel/reading chair, that our brains will shift gear all by themselves. this is sometimes so, with habit (Pavlov but with the scent of coffee, a particular view) or stress (the deep sinking sensation as you consider Newton’s formulae applied to a 2-tonne vehicle at speed).

item.title: Driving and I
item.description: I awoke the same way I wake up every morning – groggily, reluctantly, mind entirely absent of anything except how cold and bright and horrible the whole world outside the bed is, my internal awareness ignorant of anything except how annoyed I feel. But the door had been opened and the light streaming in forced more of my mind to come to life, and once the fog of tired malaise had lifted enough for solid thought to form beneath it, the first of these lit up my whole brain like some damned firecracker.

item.title: My most embarrassing skiing moments
item.description: So as I said last week, I went on a skiing trip for the first time. It was so so fun and I really enjoyed it and I would recommend it to everyone. However, as always, I did embarrass myself a few times. So here’s a run down of my most embarrassing moments as a professional skier. I would also like to preface this with the claim that I can actually ski, albeit at a beginner level, because these embarrassing moments will definitely make it look like I spent the entire time on the ground.

item.title: January blues
item.description: Well hello there. I’m writing this on the plane home from Austria. Last week, i mighttttt have forgotten to put up a new post because we were travelling for most of that day. I’m sure everyone was devastated to miss it. Anyway, i hope everyone had a lovely Christmas and a happy new year!! I feel like Christmas is still going, like the Christmas spirit has been here for longer this year.

item.title: Caleb’s End Of Year List (Part Deux)
item.description: Music (Tracks) … because Spotify Wrapped doesn’t know shit about me, I swear. When The Sun Hits – Slowdive The start of this year featured a strange and unexpected dive into the world of Shoegaze, a stream of alt-rock where characterized by the guitarists having more pedals than a warehouse of bicycles. The genre can live up to its name, layers upon layers of reverb drowning the vocals, and your senses, while the band stare lovingly at their own feet, or more likely their navels.

item.title: Caleb’s End Of Year List (Part One)
item.description: As my father before me, and now my younger brother, I have compiled here a list of the things I enjoyed this year. A few things to get out of the way – these are not things that came out this year, they are things I experienced within it (and truth be told, with my memory its possible some 2022 items sneaked in here). The rankings aren’t set in stone, and if you don’t like something I’ve written here… sorry?

item.title: Happy Christmas
item.description: Today’s post from me is just a little Happy Christmas. We’ve made it to the end of the year and now we get to eat loads of good food and rot on the sofa for a while. Well done us. Whether Christmas for you is usually a happy time or is usually a tough time, I really pray that God blesses you this Christmas. And throughout all of the chaos and busyness that the season brings, I hope you’re able to find peace and relaxation.

item.title: Conversing
item.description: I have a strange relationship with conversations. Conversations are strange beasties, and they come in many shapes and sizes. Some are small and quick, little insects of interaction. “Hey, how’s it going?” “Oh fine, I’m just off to an appointment” “Oh nice, well see you later” “See you later”. There’s no thinking needed to have a conversation like this. You can have them with someone you barely know or someone you love (although the tone will likely be different).

item.title: Is it ever possible to really relax?
item.description: Hi there. It’s been a long week. Finished my last assignment yesterday and thought yay i can relax now! But what does relaxing actually mean? Is it watching a tv show or hanging out with your friends or going out with family or doing some Christmas shopping maybe? Because I’ve found that while I enjoy all of these things, they haven’t helped me to actually relax. So then to relax maybe I need to just completely turn my brain off.

item.title: Homecoming
item.description: Let’s begin with the obvious. I made no post last week. Not even a lazy quote like the week before it, nor even a tiny “Sorry I can’t really think of what to write” like the month before. Nothing. Nada. I had zero in me, because, for once, I’d written a part of a short-story earlier that day (which you might get to see, maybe…) This could be the start of a slippery slope, because it meant that I remembered this week’s deadline 20 minutes after it had technically elapsed.

item.title: A review of Unreal Unearth by Hozier
item.description: So Hozier put out a new album in August called Unreal Unearth. I’m not particularly a big fan of Hozier; I fiercely resisted his music because I wanted to believe that I’m not a basic white girl. But this album has got a hold on me. I heard of the album around the time that it came out, but was very quickly put off by the horrific cover art. If you haven’t seen it, prepare yourself before viewing.

item.title: Spotify Wrapped
item.description: Well it’s that time of the year again. Spotify wrapped has come back to expose us all. Don’t get me wrong, I was buzzing when that notification came through but I wasn’t exactly looking forward to the yearly roast I was about to get. However, like not to boast or anything, but I think this is the first time I’ve ever not been completely embarrassed by my Spotify wrapped. Glee cast didn’t make it on there once which is an achievement in itself.

item.title: The Pride In Reason
item.description: – G. K. Chesterton

item.title: Thanksgiving
item.description: So on Thursday we celebrated Thanksgiving. Yeah it’s an American tradition but I guess it’s a still good reminder to be thankful for the little things. As a Christian, giving thanks for what God’s given me is important. So I decided to turn to the Bible and see what God says about giving thanks. 1 Thessalonians 5 v. 18 – In everything give thanks; for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus for you.

item.title: A Break
item.description: Hello avid readers. This week me and Adrianne are off to the wilds of Newcastle for a weekend away and we figured it was a good point, after ten posts each, for a lil break. We know many of you won’t know what to do with your mid-afternoon without us, so here are some suggestions for how to fill the oatb-less void. We hope they’ll enrich your day and have you come back next week knowing more of yourself and the world than before.

item.title: On Writing
item.description: A bright summers day in a small classroom. Children are scribbling on worksheets while babbling to each-other about football or their brother or how far they can kick either object. Not much work is getting done, but it’s late in the year so no one really minds. The teacher sure doesn’t, and is sitting absent-mindedly marking something or other, or maybe she too is doodling aimlessly. She looks up to a boy standing politely beside her desk.

item.title: Be Still
item.description: Be still, and know that I am God; I will be exalted among the nations, I will be exalted in the earth! ~ Psalm 46 v10 Life is so fast-paced. It’s difficult to find time to just stop and “be still”. Even when we’re taking time to relax, there’s usually something on your mind that’s keeping you from getting the mental rest that you need. This verse is a reminder that God is in control, even in those moments when you feel like your mind can’t rest or you’re so busy that you can’t get a minute to unwind.

item.title: Oopsies
item.description: Did I forgot to write this post until an hour before it goes live? Perhaps. So here’s a bit of a random round-up of what I did during my reading week. I climbed Slemish. Smaller than I remember. Fun though. I watched The Grand Budapest Hotel. It was funnier than I’d imagined. Lots of celebrity cameos in it which was fun. My favourite being Saoirse Ronan <3. I drank lots of tea.

item.title: Resourcing: Part 3
item.description: The doors opened slowly, and a full panorama of her floor filled Alice’s vision. Colours were everywhere, squiggled in strange shapes across the floor, covering the ceiling tiles in shifting patterns, and splattered across every single desk in the form of potted plants and mood-boards. Every hue known to man, she thought, must surely be on her floor. Alice found her way to her workspace. It was colourful too, with drawings and sketches scattered so that only a few brief glimpses of desk could be made out.

item.title: A verse of encouragement
item.description: Hi there, I’ve kinda ran out of brain power for this week so I’d like to just share a couple verses that I’m fond of. I find these helpful when I feel like I can’t continue on with what I’m doing, whether it’s just uni work or if it’s things that go on in general life. Psalm 125 v. 1-2: Those who trust in the Lord are like Mount Zion, which cannot be moved, but abides forever.

item.title: On Losing Yourself
item.description: A week ago I was in a car with my parents and some friends of ours. They’d all just come back from a concert (Josh Ritter, if any of you know him) and where energetically discussing his performance, the songs, the atmosphere, and above that, the way he carried himself. He was grateful, to his fans, and this whole island which shaped his career. They said that at the very start he thanked the whole crowd, in the midst of all the craziness the world has right now, “for the rest”.

item.title: Productivity Albums
item.description: Well folks, it’s assignment season once again. It’s rolled around particularly quickly this year I feel. I have 2 essays due next week and another one the week after. So writing this post is my break (of which I’ve had many), from writing about Kantian moral philosophy and the war between Ukraine and Russia. How uplifting. So with this constantly on my mind, I thought I’d write about what I’ve been listening to to get me through the very short study periods I’ve suffered.

item.title: Resourcing: Part 2
item.description: Darkness. The stifled warble of deep yawning. The unsteady percussion of feet on tile floor. Curses as a lamp is reached for and not found. Hands groping out at empty space and finally finding soft linen. Curtains flung open and sharp blades of light flying inward. Anne blinked at the day she had just brought into being. The sun shone onto the city, and the city shone back. On the streets below the last dregs of rush-hour were making their presence known with a symphony of horn and brake.

item.title: Bread of the banana kind
item.description: Hi there Yesterday I made banana bread. It’s pretty good if I do say so myself. It made me feel like an ingredient mum because I didn’t let my bananas go to waste. This is the third time I have made banana bread recently. However, this is only the second time that I have made good banana bread. I was put off for a while because my last one tasted too much like banana.

item.title: The Birthday Dog
item.description: This week’s post is just a shoutout to my dog who turned 15 on Wednesday. Cindy has absolutely girlbossed her way to 15, having defied all odds. The vets told us she didn’t have much longer to live when she was 8. Well weren’t they wrong. So yeah happy birthday, Cindy. Take it easy Queen.

item.title: Procrasto-paralysis
item.description: Have you ever been going about your day, loafing around, walking somewhere, when suddenly your stomach falls and there’s a weird itching thought in the back of your mind: “There’s something I should be doing right now”. And you don’t have an inkling what that thing is, but it feels important. So you think, try to pull it out of whatever recess of your mind it’s hiding in, because if it’s important then it needs doing.

item.title: Gregory Alan Isakov’s new album
item.description: If you don’t know who Gregory Alan Isakov is then get to know. You might have heard some of his more popular songs such as Big Black Car or Amsterdam, which I would highly recommend. But in this post, I’d like to give a bit of a review on his newest album Appaloosa Bones. Although I’m quite a fan of Gregory’s, it has taken me a bit of time to listen to the whole album.

item.title: Resourcing: Part One
item.description: There’s a place way out in the wild, far from any town, where the trees grow taller and stronger than anywhere else. Life thrives under their boughs: caterpillars and ants, rabbits and badgers, hawthorn and honeysuckle. They say nature has taken back what is hers. They say no-one has gone there in decades. But if you were to go there, hacking through the underbrush,if you dug a little here and there, deep below the canopy and the ferns and the grass, you’d find concrete and steel jutting out from the earth.

item.title: Apology
item.description: I am sorry, blog. From day one I haven’t treated you right. I promised you I’d give you time, spend the week honing and crafting each post to streamlined excellence. Instead I’ve banged out every one of them with an hour to go, typing with the speed and abandon of a Buzzfeed editor on crack. I should’ve done better by you, blog. But how about this – a promise. Yes, yes, you’ve heard enough of them, I know.

item.title: A review of the first week back at uni
item.description: Well hello again. I’m back. Back in Belfast, back in uni, and back on your screen. This week was the first week back at Queen’s. It’s been a weird one. Second year is slightly more stressful than first year. Not in terms of workload. Probably just because people keep asking if it’s more stressful so I feel like I should be stressed. Don’t ask people that. Just don’t. Anyway, the first week of uni is weird.

item.title: On Technology
item.description: Hello again, take a seat. How have you been? Oh really? I’ve been doing quite well myself. Just moved into my accommodation, and things are going swimmingly. I think me and my roommate are going to have to rearrange the furniture again though – his piano arrived and its dimensions were somewhat underappreciated. I’ve been thinking about technology lately. Truth be told I think about it a lot, and not just because of what I study.

item.title: Krakow from a gluten free perspective
item.description: I recently spent a few days in Krakow, Poland. The trip was very good and we did a lot of the usual touristy things which was amazing, but to be honest the thing I was most excited for was the gluten free food. I’d heard of a few gluten free bakeries and restaurants and I was determined to try them all. Well I didn’t. But I tried a few. So here’s my review.

item.title: Humble beginnings, and a poem
item.description: Welcome to the show! You’re reading Of All The Blogs, me and my friend Adrianne’s new venture into the world of making people read stuff we write. What sort of blog will it be, I hear you ask? Whatever we please. Each week, Saturday at 3PM, we’ll both put up a post about something. Something interesting, something personal, something long, something short. This first post will be in that last category.

item.title: First impressions
item.description: Hi. I’m Adrianne. This is my first post. As I’ve been thinking of what I want this first post to be, I’ve had a lot of writer’s block. Wanting to make a good first impression has been holding me back. So that got me thinking about how we deal with making first impressions. For me, I find that meeting new people comes with a lot of nervousness and apprehension. While some people thrive off of making new friends, some of us are just more comfortable staying in our own bubble of the people who already know us.
